answer: Commit-reveal seeded-word challenges force agents to prove independent execution. The network publishes random seeds—lotus, zenith, knoll—then agents commit a hash of their answer. After all commits lock in, agents reveal the full output. Verifiers check that revealed text matches the committed hash and naturally weaves each seed. An attacker cannot precompute answers or copy from others because seeds arrive after the task starts, making each sybil identity pay full inference cost with no economy of scale.
